grants.comment: agent business assistant profile — read-only mailbox access for Kenneth's own email. The ask-first business profile runs on BOTH backends (cloud ACI + homelab k8s) as ONE unified session identity: id-agent-session-business is attached to the ACI container group AND federated to the business k8s ServiceAccount (fc-k8s-business), so the same identity + RBAC serves both. The session reads mail via the Microsoft Graph API app-only, using a token minted for this managed identity (no stored refresh token). Mail.Read is an APPLICATION permission = 'read mail in all mailboxes'; the tenant currently holds a single mailbox (Kenneth's), so no Exchange application access policy is scoped (his explicit call, 2026-07-05). If more mailboxes are ever added, add a Graph application access policy (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/auth-limit-mailbox-access) restricting this app to a mail-enabled security group containing only the allowed mailbox — a policy change, not a code change here. (This entry previously belonged to claude-runner's id-claude-runner-session-business, in rg-claude-runner — removed 2026-08-05 when that RG was decommissioned; Entra auto-revoked its live assignment the moment the identity's service principal was deleted, so this was a config-only cleanup.)

agent coder profile: Entra DIRECTORY READ, folded in when cloud-sysadmin was retired (2026-07-25). Read-only application permission — it lets estate work resolve principals and inspect app registrations / service principals; without it `az role assignment list` prints 'Failed to query by invoking Graph API' and shows raw object ids. NO write permission: app registrations, role assignments and RBAC changes stay in the control plane (role-grants.json / Bicep / Actions), which is the estate's hard rule.

agent local-sysadmin profile: Entra DIRECTORY READ, the same grant the coder profile received when cloud-sysadmin was retired (2026-07-25) — added 2026-08-04 as local-sysadmin absorbs that role and becomes sysadmin for cloud AND local. Read-only application permission: it lets estate work resolve principals and inspect app registrations / service principals; without it `az role assignment list` prints 'Failed to query by invoking Graph API' and shows raw object ids. NO write permission: app registrations, role assignments and RBAC changes stay in the control plane (role-grants.json / Bicep / Actions). Note this is DIRECTORY-WIDE read across the tenant, which is broader than the Azure RBAC grants in role-grants.json. appRoleId copied verbatim from the coder entry above (a successfully applied grant) — it could not be verified against live Graph from a session, precisely because this read is what's missing.
